scope: Proposition 3.2 (Affine-distance and Gram bounds) of the manuscript “Memory and precision in noiseless Gaussian regression” (preprints/Memory-and-precision-in-noiseless-Gaussian-regression-September-27-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 140 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 a46ccc95821da009), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 8. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: Under the assumptions of Theorem 3.1, use the factors Jj defined there. If L is an affine j-plane with 0 ≤ j ≤ p − 2, then, for 0 < t ≤ R, µ{s : dist(s, L) ≤ t} ≤ 3j 2β HRj tβ−j , (12) Z dist(s, L)−m dµ(s) ≤ JjHRβ−m . (13) For a tuple (s1, . . . , sp), let V = [s2 − s1, . . . , sp − s1]. The matrix V has full column rank for µ⊗p-almost every tuple, and Z det(V T V )−m/2 dµ⊗p ≤ Hp Rβp−m(p−1) p−2 Y j=0 Jj. (14) The integrand in (14) may be assigned any value on the null set of rank-deficient tuples.
